data.text: [00:03]Good evening and thank you for coming to find out about the Hillside Survival School. `[00:09]My name’s David Johnson. I started the school and I’m the school’s chief instructor. `[00:15]I learned my survival skills while I was in the army and before starting the Hillside Survival School, I worked in other well-known survival schools.

[00:25]So, first, why do people come on our courses? `[00:29.8]What are our aims? Well, firstly, we aim to help people to discover nature and the outdoor life … and to remind people that there is more to life than city living. `[00:41]Secondly, and perhaps more importantly, we want people to work well as a team and to have fun together … and a lot of people come to do just that!

[00:52]Who comes on our courses? Who are our courses for? Well, the answer is anybody and everybody. `[01:00]We get a lot of groups of colleagues – people who work together, like you. `[01:06]The weekend courses are a fantastic way of team-building, and having fun together, as I said. `[01:11.9]The courses are also popular with groups of friends who want to do something a bit more challenging than lying on a beach!

[01:20]So, let me tell you about what happens on some of our courses …. `[01:25]The most popular course we run is our basic survival course which lasts a weekend and takes place throughout the year. `[01:33.9]This course teaches you the basic skills that you need to survive in the wilderness and costs a hundred and seventy-five pounds per person. `[01:43]Choose this one and you will have the best weekend you’ve ever had!

[01:47]If you want an even bigger challenge, our extreme survival course takes place between November and February when the conditions are more difficult. `[01:57]These courses also last for a weekend and cost a hundred and ninety-five pounds per person. `[02:03.3]The extreme survival course teaches you to survive in a wet and cold environment. `[02:09.9]In fact, we aim to give you the wettest, coldest weekend ever!

[02:15]The course offers you the chance to push yourself, both physically and mentally. No tents, no gas cookers; just you and the wilderness. `[02:25.4]You learn to find food and cook it over an open fire. `[02:29]You learn to build a shelter and then you actually sleep in it. It could be the hardest thing you’ve ever done by far – you won’t have the most comfortable weekend of your life, but you will probably be surprised how well you can cope with difficult conditions.

[02:45]Well … thank you very much for inviting me here to your company to tell you about Hillside Survival School. `[02:53.8]If you’re interested in doing any of our courses with a group of colleagues, speak to your manager. `[02:59]You can also pick up a booklet before you go ... it includes information about all the courses, prices, dates and application forms. `[03:07.5]Push yourself – it really could be the best thing you’ve ever done! ... And, yes, I think we’ve got time for a few questions ... before you all get back to work. … Erm … yes … the er, the man at the back …
